title: Rotator Cuff Repair Rehabilitation
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Tear size, tendons repaired, tissue quality, other procedures (biceps tenodesis, acromioplasty), surgeon's protocol and sling time (commonly around 4 to 6 weeks).
qa: Why is tendon-to-bone healing slow? Tendon attaches to bone through a complex zone with limited blood supply.
What is safe in phase 1? Elbow, wrist, hand exercises, pendulum and passive range within limits.
What suggests a re-tear? Sudden pain and loss of active elevation after an incident.
Why move the elbow and hand early? To prevent stiffness and swelling.
When does strengthening usually start? Often around 12 weeks, per the surgeon.

redFlags.Finding: Sudden pain and loss of active movement after an incident
Increasing stiffness in all directions, severe night pain
Hand swelling, colour change, burning pain

exerciseNotes: Pendulum; supine passive elevation using the other arm; table slides; wand external rotation (within limits); isometrics (when allowed); band external and internal rotation; side-lying external rotation; scapular retraction; progressive elevation with weights; functional and sport-specific training.
pathway: Early versus delayed motion: both approaches show similar long-term outcomes in many trials; early motion may improve early range, with some concern about healing in large tears.
